item.title: Aaron Rodgers releases new statement via Al Michaels, says he went on 'Pat McAfee Show' after Steelers barred him from team facility
item.description: Aaron Rodgers made quite a few waves on his way out of the Pittsburgh Steelers earlier this week. He had more to say during their first game without him. Prime Video broadcaster Al Michaels relayed a text message he got from the former MVP during the Steelers’ game against the Denver Broncos, which served to rebut some of his critics and explain why he handled things the way he did. Michaels read the text messages early in the fourth quarter of the Black Friday game. Al Michaels reads a message he received from Aaron Rodgers earlier today. pic.twitter.com/4ijFB2wFnN — NFL on Prime Video (@NFLonPrime) November 27, 2026 First, Rodgers complained about the idea he has committed some sort of locker room faux pas by airing out dirty laundry involving Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy, whom Rodgers accused of a number of shortcomings during an appearance on “The Pat McAfee Show” on Wednesday: “A lot of talk about the sanctity of the locker room … The code or sanctity exists to protect the integrity of the locker room, not to provide immunity from accountability for its leadership.” That rebuttal could be aimed at a number of notable figures. Rodgers’ quarterbacking peer Tom Brady said “ The sanctity of an NFL locker room, it's a very sacred place. ” Rodgers’ former coach Mike Tomlin said it was sad “to see laundry aired out that way in a public forum, those are things that kind of run counterculture to professional football.” Steelers owner Art Rooney II said, “ In general, I think, historically, what's in the locker room stays in the locker room. That's the way it's always been. That's the way it should be as far as I'm concerned. ” Former Steelers quarterbacks Terry Bradshaw and Russell Wilson both expressed their disapproval . Aaron Rodgers still has something to say after the NFL's loudest divorce. AP Photo/Terrance Williams As for how things played out with the Steelers, it’s known that Rodgers made some sort of ultimatum — reportedly that he wanted to call plays on offense or be released — and the Steelers opted to announce his benching late Tuesday night then release him Wednesday after he aired his grievances against McCarthy. Rodgers claimed he got no communication from McCarthy until his benching was announced, and that he only appeared on McAfee after the Steelers barred him from their facility: “They took this public, never heard from the head coach, then they leak at 11:00 p.m. They also barred me from the facility. That's why I went to McAfee." Odds are this won’t be the last time we hear about Rodgers on this. Meanwhile, his former teammates defeated the Broncos 27-5 on Friday behind a dominant defensive performance . Rodgers did appears to receive a shout-out from wide receiver DK Metcalf, though .

With all the drama surrounding the Steelers, many thought the Broncos were in line to get their ninth victory of the season. Alas, that wasn’t the case and Denver was shellacked on the road by Pittsburgh 27-5. Here are some instant reactions from today’s matchup. Murphy’s Law was in full effect in Broncos’ embarrassing loss Anything that could have possibly went wrong for the Broncos this afternoon did. For all the talk about the Steelers potentially coming out flat , the exact opposite transpired. It was Denver who came out of the gate absolutely lifeless. Quarterback Bo Nix played the worst game of his career. We have seen him perform bad in the elements the past two seasons. However, today’s awfulness was on an entirely different level. Early on, Nix had a fumble that resulted in a touchdown for the Steelers in the first quarter. At the end of the second quarter, he threw an errant pass that was picked off by cornerback Jalen Ramsey and returned for a touchdown. You can’t spot an opposing team fourteen points. As I wrote earlier today, winning the turnover battle was going to be mission critical for the Broncos. They certainly wound up on the wrong side of that equation. Of course, the poor weather didn’t help matters. That being said, it’s no excuse for how poor he and the offense played today. It was absolutely dreadful from start to finish. On defense, even Patrick Surtain II had an off day, and those rarely ever happen. Overall, I’m still quite perplexed at how off kilter the Broncos looked. item.title: Henry Cejudo reflects on passing of Eddie Cha: ‘Master Cha, you will always be remembered’
item.description: Henry Cejudo and Eddie Cha worked closely for years Henry Cejudo is going to miss Eddie Cha. On Wednesday, Cha, the famed striking coach at Fight Ready in Glendale, Ariz., died suddenly of unknown causes . During his career, Cha worked with some of the biggest names in MMA, but arguably his most successful student is former UFC flyweight and bantamweight champion Henry Cejudo. Speaking with MMA Fighting’s Mike Heck ahead of RAF 15, Cejudo reacted to the sudden passing of his longtime coach. “It hurts,” Cejudo said. “It’s sad. I don’t know if you guys remember when Kobe died, Kobe Bryant—obviously he wasn’t Kobe Bryant, known by the world, but the people that loved him, something just doesn’t sit right. … 53 years old. Great man, great husband, great coach, great friend, and it’s just too bad. He’s too young to leave. But we never know when it’s our turn. Life is life. It’s just unfortunate. It’s very sad. … “I know Eddie would want us to continue, keep pushing forward, and I’m going to honor Eddie this weekend with this victory.” Cha was a significant figure in Cejudo’s MMA career, shepherding the Olympic wrestling champion’s transition to MMA striking. Cejudo gave one example of just how much of an impact Cha had on him. “He brought a lot of the traditional Tae Kwon Do style of ‘Yes, sir. Yes, mister.’ Just respecting your elders type of thing,” Cejudo said. “And he would always—very kind in that sense, and he would give you the small little bow, whether you’re an elder, he would open the door for you, things like that. You could tell he comes from a really good tradition of how he was raised through martial arts. “I think the biggest thing with Eddie, he came up with the game plan when I beat Dominick Cruz. We started getting the feel—and you could hear it, too. You can see when I gave him a shoutout right after the fight. They gave me the post-fight mic with Joe Rogan, and I was just like, ‘Hey man, that was all Eddie Cha,’ and it was, because he was just smart. He was like, ‘Dominick moves his upper body a lot; he’s hard to hit up top, but Henry, look what he leaves behind: his legs.’ So we kicked the crap out of his legs. So that was something that I really started to do because of Eddie. “I think everybody has an impact in your life, and Eddie is definitely one of them. I’m just heartbroken, still. But I know what Eddie would want. He’s like, ‘Dude, keep moving forward.’ He was there when my sister died; he gave me great advice, and things like that. Guys were always there. Condolences to him and his family and everybody that loved him. Eddie Cha, Master Cha, you will always be remembered.” Cejudo competes in the main event of RAF 15 on Saturday, defending his lightweight crossover title against past MMA opponent Song Yadong.

item.title: Mizzou Heads Into December on 6-Game Win Streak After UAPB Win
item.description: Nov 27, 2026; Columbia, Missouri, USA; Missouri Tigers forward Bryson Tiller (15) shoots a layup against the Arkansas-Pine Bluff Golden Lions during the first half of the game at Mizzou Arena. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Arkansas-Pine Bluff completed the last domino in Missouri men’s basketball’s mid-major homestand. When you’re the worst team ranked by KenPom, a bad game must be the norm. The Tigers came into the Friday afternoon game as a 38-point favorite and walked out just under that line with a 97-61 win against the Golden Lions. After a closer-than-expected 78-67 win over Evansville Tuesday night, Mizzou had to right some wrongs before a loaded December slate that includes four teams currently ranked in the AP Top 25. The changes started even before tipoff against the Golden Lions when Mark Mitchell was announced in the starting lineup in place of Kennard Davis Jr. Mitchell hadn’t started since suffering a concussion in the opening minute against SIUE on Nov. 9. The fifth-year forward injected life into the offense with 14 points, three rebounds and three assists on 6-for-8 shooting. All of his shots came from inside the arc, an area where the Tigers saw great success. Mizzou had a dominant performance inside the arc with 50 points in the paint and shot 74.6% on two-point attempts. The interior presence also came with trips to the free-throw line. The Tigers went 24-for-27 from the charity stripe as a team. Bryson Tiller contributed nine makes on 10 attempts in what was one of his most dominant performances of the season. The Kansas transfer finished the game with 22 points on 6-for-10 shooting to go with six rebounds and four blocks. Tiller only missed one shot inside the arc. Paint success once again came at the expense of another off-night from three-point range. Jason Crowe Jr. made all three of Mizzou’s triples in a 16.7% outside shooting night as a team, and it nearly replicated that performance against the Golden Lions. The Tigers went 5-for-20 from beyond the arc after beginning the first half shooting 3-for-4 from deep. Mizzou still adopted the big brother role to UAPB from the tip by securing six points off three turnovers less than two minutes into the game. It finished the game with 23 points off 18 turnovers. Toni Bryant and Trent Pierce set the tone on multiple defensive possessions. Bryant finished the night with seven blocks and could consistently be heard throughout Mizzou Arena with his active communication. The freshman also contributed 14 points, eight rebounds and four assists. Pierce continues to struggle offensively, but he’s playable because of his defensive impact. He ended the night with four steals and a block despite only scoring two points on three shots. The Tigers still have plenty to clean up ahead of what may be their biggest test of the season to this point. They host Pittsburgh at 6 p.m. Tuesday. The Panthers are currently 8-0 and ranked 35th in KenPom.

(Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos were blown out by the Pittsburgh Steelers on Black Friday, which has some big impacts on the AFC Playoff Picture. With this loss, the Broncos’ odds of winning the number one seed in the AFC have taken a big hit, and it also keeps the Chiefs within striking range for the AFC West. The Broncos still do have a favorable schedule upcoming and play the Bills, but no Broncos fan is thinking one seed after a loss like this. With the Chiefs’ loss on Thanksgiving Night, the Broncos still lead the AFC West but both teams are tied at 8-3. As for the Steelers, their wild week continues. It looks like they imploded. Aaron Rodgers was released, McCarthy was embarrassed on National Television, and the locker room appeared to be in disarray. Well, that all changed on Friday when they came out and absolutely dominated the Broncos at home, improved to 7-4, and kept their playoff hopes very alive. They move up to the 6th seed right now, but that could change after the weekend finishes. Looking ahead to the rest of the games this weekend, the Bengals play the Saints, the Jaguars play the Titans, and the Browns play on Sunday Night vs. the Raiders. item.title: Winners, Losers from Pittsburgh Steelers’ Statement 27-5 Win Over Denver Broncos on Black Friday
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Aaron Rodgers made himself and head coach Mike McCarthy the story of the National Football League ahead of Thanksgiving, overshadowing an important Denver Broncos vs. Pittsburgh Steelers game on Black Friday that had major playoff implications. What we saw today probably shows why everyone is better off now that Rodgers will fade away into a darkness retreat where we never hear from him again. Let’s dive into the winners and losers from the Broncos vs Steelers matchup on Black Friday, with Pittsburgh making a massive statement with a 22-point win. Winner: Mike McCarthy, Pittsburgh Steelers Head Coach Nov 22, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy on the sidelines against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images An overwhelming majority of the reactions league-wide to what Rodgers said about Mike McCarthy defended the kind of person McCarthy was. It was noticeable that many of the accusations made against the Steelers head coach weren’t rebuffed. After having his play-calling, game preparation and work ethic all called out on a national stage, McCarthy desperately needed to respond on the field. He did just that. Against a top-10 defense, the Steelers offense backed up its head coach and play-caller where it counts. In the first half alone, the Steelers offense had nearly as many total yards (132) as it had in the first half of its last two games combined (139) with Rodgers. Pittsburgh’s defense also seemed quite motivated to come through for its head coach, scoring two touchdowns on its own with two sacks and zero red-zone trips allowed to Denver in the first half. Clearly, the entire Steelers locker room is happy to keep playing and winning for McCarthy. Meanwhile… Loser: Aaron Rodgers Nov 22, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) leaves the field after the game at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Aaron Rodgers is going to be a first-ballot Hall of Famer and rightfully remembered years from now as one of the most gifted quarterbacks in NFL history. He should also be known moving forward for causing one of, if not the most, disastrous ends to a legendary playing career in the history of pro sports. When you have your head coach last year (Mike Tomlin), former teammates (Greg Jennings, T.J. Lang and James Jones) along with your well-respected peers (Tom Brady) all rip you for how you handled your exit and trying to sabotage McCarthy’s coaching career, that speaks volumes about your reputation. Fittingly, it was made even worse for Rodgers by the fact that the Steelers responded to Rodgers’ exit by immediately putting up 14 points against Denver. item.title: Houston Texans welcome back Woody Marks and Marvin Harrison Jr. as offense gets a boost Sunday
item.description: Houston Texans running back Woody Marks (4) runs the ball against Cleveland Browns cornerback Denzel Ward (21) during the first half of an NFL football game in Cleveland, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. (Brett Coomer/Houston Chronicle) Houston Texans running back Woody Marks and wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. will return Sunday against the Baltimore Ravens. Marks missed last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts with a concussion, while Harrison missed the past two games with a hamstring injury. "I just want to help the team win games," Harrison said. "At the end of the day, that's why every person, every player is here on this team." Harrison has six catches in three games since the Texans acquired him after their Week 5 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars to bolster their receiving corps. He hasn't been an immediate difference-maker for Houston, but he also wasn't expected to quickly take on a heavy workload as he learned the Texans' system. Harrison played fewer than 21% of the team's snaps in each of his first two games before his share jumped to 45% against the Los Angeles Chargers in his third game. Harrison said he continued learning the playbook while recovering from his injury and feels very good about his understanding of it. "Getting him back right now is a perfect time to get him rolling," Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud said. "He's been running great routes. I think everybody's been seeing that. Have to find ways to get him to rock. I think he's doing a great job creating separation and we'll continue to do that for us." Marks' return will mark the first time in nearly two months that Houston's top two running backs will enter a game healthy. David Montgomery returned from an injury of his own last week against the Colts. Montgomery, who had struggled for most of the season outside of a standout Week 1, rushed for more than 100 yards in the win. In the five games before missing the Colts game with an injury, Marks averaged more than 60 yards per game. How the Texans will split their snaps is unclear, but offensive coordinator Nick Caley said earlier in the week that having both players back is good for the team. "When we run the ball, everybody just needs to handle their assignment the right way," coach DeMeco Ryans said Wednesday. "We'll get a ton of different looks this week from the Ravens. We just have to make sure we're communicating the right way." While those two key pieces will be back Sunday, Houston's offense won't be fully healthy. Wide receiver Kayshon Boutte is out with a hip injury, while left guard Keylan Rutledge also will be unavailable with neck and shoulder injuries. item.title: Max Melton calls out Arizona Cardinals as defense searches for answers
item.description: Shortly before the Arizona Cardinals ’ final practice of the week on Friday, Nov. 27, cornerback Max Melton took to social media to voice his latest round of frustration. “I do something to somebody?” wrote Melton, who played zero defensive snaps last week for the first time in his career. Later, inside the Cardinals locker room, Melton explained the source of his discontent. “I don't know what I did to get my time taken away,” Melton said. “I feel like I was having a really good season. That's pretty much it. I asked. I'm yet to get a clear answer. (Expletive) That was really it. I thought I was having a good season. Shooting 1000%? No way. But 90s? Yeah.” On the season, Melton has allowed 19 catches for 201 yards and two touchdowns on 33 targets, per Pro Football Focus. His passer rating when targeted is 95.6 — better than Denzel Burke, but trailing behind Kei’Tel Clark. That number had also ticked up in recent weeks. To start the season, Melton had four pass breakups in five games, performing at the highest level of any Cardinals cornerback. But over the past month, he was culpable for a handful of big plays as his snap share gradually decreased, culminating in last week’s full-time move to the bench. Melton, though, was not alone with his occasional miscues. In the final few games under Nick Rallis, few Cardinals defensive players delivered standout performances. "I haven't got a clear answer to what I've done to get removed," Melton said. "What I have to do to get back out there? I'm just sticking to a normal routine, still making plays in practice, still paying attention in meetings, still doing everything I think is right. But I don't know. I'm just kind of lost and frustrated." Melton said that he had been hoping his role would expand after the Cardinals fired Rallis this week, installing Teryl Austin as their interim defensive coordinator. That, however, has not happened, as the Cardinals seemingly plan to once again deploy Burke and Clark as their starting outside cornerbacks. “It's still early,” Melton said. “We've only been out here a couple days. So immediate change, maybe not. But I don't know. I'm just confused. I thought I was having a good season. It's frustrating.” Despite his frustration, Melton was able to impress on special teams last week, taking three kick returns for 103 yards. He also downed a punt inside the five-yard line. “I love special teams,” Melton said. “I'm from (Rutgers coach) Greg Schiano. Anything to help the team. I still love the guys and stuff like that. Still support and do whatever I can so we can win. But I love special teams. You see them out returning. I always wanted to do that.” Still, it’s hardly the role either Melton or the Cardinals envisioned when he was selected 43rd overall in the 2024 draft. But that level of squandered capital has been a common theme for the Cardinals. item.title: Comeback, Commence: Panthers Score in Final Minute, Stun Capitals
item.description: The Florida Panthers trailed the host Capitals by a goal with less than 5 minutes remaining to play on Friday. Then, the comeback commenced. Eetu Luostarinen tied the score off a pass from Brad Marchand before Matthew Tkachuk ’s shot was knocked in by Sam Bennett with 23.2 seconds left leading the Panthers to a 3-2 win. With the win, the Panthers slid into second place in the Atlantic Division what with Tampa Bay getting blown out at home to the Senators. The Panthers will fly home to face the Lightning in Sunrise on Saturday night. Cole Hutson became the fastest defenseman in Capitals history to hit 10 goals in the first period against the Panthers on Friday afternoon. In the third, Hutson got to 11. Hutson’s two goals gave the Capitals a 2-1 lead before the Panthers started their comebacl. Aaron Ekblad tied the score with a booming goal on the power play in the second. Jacob Markstrom ended with 24 saves. NOTES: PANTHERS AT CAPITALS Aaron Ekblad tied the game with his 43rd career power-play goal which pulled him within one such goal of tying Pavel Bure and Jonathan Huberdeau for sixth place on the franchise’s all-time list . Garnet Hathaway left the game early in the third after he and Dylan Strome collided in open ice. Hathaway appeared to get hit on his left knee. HOW THEY SCORED Capitals 1, Panthers 0 (10:26 1st): Cole Hutson sends a wrist shot from the high slot past Jacob Markstrom. Panthers 1, Capitals 1 (4:51 2nd PP): Aaron Ekblad sends a blast on a one-timer that beats Logan Thompson . item.title: Chelsea in a 'difficult moment' admits Alonso
item.description: Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso reacts after the 3-2 defeat at Nottingham Forest (Darren Staples) Xabi Alonso admitted Chelsea are in a "difficult moment" as the beleaguered boss urged his struggling side to stick together after their dismal 3-2 defeat at Nottingham Forest on Friday. Alonso's side crashed to a third successive Premier League loss to leave them languishing in eighth place. The Blues have lost four of their last five league matches, piling pressure on Alonso just months into his reign at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea fell behind to Igor Jesus's early opener before Morgan Gibbs-White doubled Forest's lead with a second half penalty. Emmanuel Emegha reduced the deficit but Gibbs-White struck again to make Emega's late second nothing more than a footnote on another dispiriting evening for Alonso. "It's a difficult moment for everyone. It's disappointing again to lose again but we need to keep trying to find solutions, we can't stop," Alonso said. "We are low in confidence, the team is struggling to hold a result. After getting to 2-1 we have conceded and go to 3-1. "Everything is not going our way, we are responsible for that and we are responsible to find solutions." Chelsea have already conceded 23 goals in 12 league matches and their porous defence was not helped by Alonso's curious decision to use Ecuador midfielder Moises Caicedo in a back-three. Alonso also selected Wesley Fofana after the centre-back was forced to apologise for joking in a YouTube interview about missing a penalty during Chelsea's League Cup defeat against Liverpool this season. The hapless Fofana was booed by angry Chelsea fans at the City Ground and conceded a penalty with his careless foul on former Blues striker Liam Delap. "We need to support everyone. Everyone that is in the team we need to support," Alonso said of Fofana. "We know we have to go through difficult moments. We don't take apart anyone and we want to help." Asked to assess Chelsea's dismal run, Alonso suggested the only cure was hard work on the training ground. "We can do better for sure. At this level you need to hold results and that is why we are losing in the last games," he said after Chelsea's sixth league defeat his term. "That is the only way I understand football. When things are not going well, try to work and find solutions. It can happen that we turn it around and it goes our way." Chelsea's sixth league defeat under Alonso will spark pointed questions about the former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen boss. Although Alonso led Leverkusen to an historic Bundesliga title in 2024, he lasted just seven months before being sacked by Real. The former Liverpool midfielder desperately needs a win against bottom of the table Crystal Palace on Wednesday to avoid the sack talk growing even louder. "Everyone needs to stick together and go through this moment. We have to deal with it," he said. smg/bsp

item.title: Aaron Rodgers Fires Back Following Tom Brady’s Locker Room Comments
item.description: Aaron Rodgers isn’t ready to let his ugly divorce from the Pittsburgh Steelers go quietly. On Friday, the former Steelers quarterback offered another public defense of his controversial decision to air his grievances with head coach Mike McCarthy during an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show . Just one day after Tom Brady weighed in on the importance of protecting the sanctity of an NFL locker room, Rodgers offered a decidedly different perspective. This time, he delivered his message through legendary NFL broadcaster Al Michaels. Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) prepares to throw a pass in the third quarter of the NFL Week 10 game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Aaron Rodgers Pushes Back on Locker Room Criticism During the fourth quarter of Friday’s game between the Steelers and Denver Broncos, Michaels read a text message from Rodgers addressing the criticism he has received. According to Pro Football Talk , Rodgers believes protecting the locker room should not come at the expense of holding coaches accountable. “A lot of talk about the sanctity of the locker room,” Rodgers said in the text. “The code or sanctity exists to protect the integrity of the locker room, not to provide immunity from accountability for its leadership. They took this public. Never heard from the head coach. Then they leaked at 11 p.m. They also barred me from the facility. That’s why I went to McAfee.” Rodgers’ comments come after he made several stunning allegations about McCarthy , including claims that the coach slept during meetings and mistakenly referred to the Steelers as the Packers during halftime of Sunday’s game. Aaron Rodgers and Tom Brady Clearly See Things Differently During Thursday’s Eagles-Cowboys broadcast, Brady criticized Rodgers for making private matters public . The seven-time Super Bowl champion emphasized that individual interests should never supersede what a team is trying to accomplish. Brady wasn’t alone in his criticism, as several former NFL players expressed similar concerns during Thanksgiving broadcasts. Rodgers did not specifically mention Brady in his text to Michaels, but his choice of words certainly appeared to address the growing criticism. Meanwhile, the Steelers were dominating the Broncos when Michaels shared Rodgers’ message. For McCarthy, winning football games may be the most effective response of all.

item.description: LAFC fight for MLS Cup Playoffs survival vs. St. Louis CITY By Ari Liljenwall With their season on the line, LAFC must turn the tide in Game 2 of their Western Conference Round One Best-of-3 Series against St. Louis CITY SC . After suffering a 3-2 defeat at Energizer Park in Game 1, the Black & Gold return home to BMO Stadium on Saturday (8:30 pm ET | Apple TV ) needing a victory to force a decisive Game 3 in St. Louis on Dec. 2. Despite the series-opening setback, interim head coach Xavi Tamarit was encouraged by his team's response in recent days. “The week has been very good, a very good week of training," Tamarit told reporters Friday. “I feel the players [have] the confidence that we can do it, so that gives me a lot of confidence. “We know they are a very good team," he added. "They have a lot of weapons, but we do also. We feel that we didn't have an amazing game the other day, and we were very close to drawing at the end when, in the last 30 minutes, we started to play better.” Backs against the wall While LAFC never found an equalizer in Game 1, they showed resilience in the second half. Via tallies from Sergi Palencia and Denis Bouanga , the Black & Gold twice pulled within a goal after trailing by two, giving them something to build on heading into Saturday's must-win match. “Of course, we have to go for the win from the first [minute], but we cannot lose our organization,” Tamarit said. “We have to be intelligent. “We have to win the game in many ways, and we have to know that it's not a game that's going to finish in the 15th minute.” Despite boasting two of the league's most dangerous attackers in Bouanga and South Korean icon Son Heung-Min , LAFC know they'll need to be sharper on both sides of the ball to keep their season alive. “The talent and quality is not enough. The Gabon international also acknowledged the team's struggles to maintain their discipline when playing from behind. “When we concede one goal, we want to forget everything,” added Bouanga. Home comforts Perhaps the biggest reason for optimism is LAFC's return to BMO Stadium, where they'll have the backing of their home supporters as they look to extend their postseason run. Tamarit believes his players are eager to make amends for their Game 1 defeat. “I think the game is going to be different than the other day. item.title: How the opening night of Nations Championship finals weekend fell flat
item.description: It had been billed as a three-day Super Bowl of rugby but the grand opening of the Nations Championship finals weekend fell short of such lofty comparisons. Sparsely attended, bitterly cold, a few television technical gremlins – one always feared this Friday night would be a tough sell and so it proved. Not many more than 30,000 spectators made it in to watch Ireland complete a November clean sweep with victory over Australia, and far fewer for Italy’s narrow win over Fiji that preceded it. Ireland overcame Australia at a sparsely-attended Twickenham (AP) With those results came a 2-0 lead for the north in the race for the “Hemisphere Shield”, though that the organisers spent much of the night clarifying that these were not placing play-offs said plenty about a competition still yet to truly cut through. Colossal contests await over the weekend as the southern hemisphere powers seek revenge on their northern foes, but neither England vs New Zealand nor the grand final between France and South Africa is expected to draw a full house. There was an admirable effort at razzmatazz wrapped around the logistical challenges that a double-header poses – but this first of three consecutive rugby-laden days suggested an imperfect idea that requires some refinement. A neutral site detracted from, rather than enhanced, the occasion. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville.
